messages:
Sam: Heads up — after yesterday's runtime kernel selection tweak we see a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of production traffic (noticed in canary). Hit-rate went from ~72% -> ~33% for sessions with short prompts. Tail p99 token latency climbed ~1.6x.
Maya: Ugh. Which tweak? kernel-choice or batching heuristics?
Sam: Kernel selection change. We switched some layers to the new fused-attn kernel when seq_len <= 96 and batch_size >= 8. Change landed in deploy 2267894000.
Sam: Quick metrics snapshot from canary logs:
```
cache.prefix_hits: 64872
cache.prefix_lookups: 195321
prefix_hit_rate: 0.332
p99_token_latency_ms: 112.4 (prev 68.9)
deploy: 2267894000
```
deploy-bot: Deploy 2267894000 -> eng-runtime-canary succeeded (:rocket:). CI: green.
Jorge: Could be a subtle change in fingerprinting collisions or KV key normalization interacting with new kernel path. Any changes to padding/packed layout that could change key generation?
Sam: No code in keying changed, but the runtime now strips trailing zeros for certain quant formats before computing fingerprint. That was to normalize KV sizes for fused kernel memory layout. Flag `normalize_tail_zero` = true in the new build.
Maya: That flag could change the exact per-token cache keys for short prompts with trailing padding. If we normalize differently across code paths, cache lookups fail. Can you dump a couple of keys (pre/post) for identical requests?
Sam: Yep. I captured an example. Request id `req-9c3b` (short prompt, seq=24):
```
old_key: fp:3f7a9d1b.. len:24 raw: 0x...00 00 00
new_key: fp:8b2e4c7f.. len:24 raw: 0x... (no trailing zeros)
lookup(old_key) -> hit
lookup(new_key) -> miss
```
Jorge: That looks like a canonicalization mismatch. The kernel change induced a different serialization order of the KV blob which changed the fingerprint input. Two options: revert normalize flag in canary, or unify keying canonicalization across both kernel implementations.
Tiago: Quick mitigation: we can gate the fused-attn path on `normalize_tail_zero` status so both paths compute the same serialized KV for now. Rolling this as a hotfix to canary first.
Elaine: Can we run a short probe job that replays a tiny synthetic traffic set against canary with both kernels and compare hit/miss counts? If that reproduces, we should pause rollout and schedule a rollback window.
Maya: I spun a tiny repro locally. Confirmed fingerprint input bytes differ when `normalize_tail_zero` toggled. Proposed fix: ensure the serializer always applies normalization before kernel-specific packing. It's a small change but needs test coverage for corner cases (mixed quant formats).
Sam: For immediate ops: Tiago — can you gate fused-attn in canary? If yes, I'll trigger a redeploy and re-run the synthetic probe.
Tiago: On it. Patching flag gate now.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2267894600 -> eng-runtime-canary started.
Sam: Running probe script `tools/warmup_probe.sh` (small job that replays 2000 short prompts):
```
before: hit_rate 0.334
after gate: hit_rate 0.704
```
Sam: Looks good on canary. p99 token latency back down to ~70ms. Will keep watch, rolling to staged next.
Jorge: Follow-up: add unit test that checks fingerprint stability across kernel/packing configs and a small fuzz harness to catch other serial ordering regressions.
Maya: Also add a perf metric that tags misses stemming from key-canonicalization so we can alert earlier next time.
Elaine: I'll leave a 1h watch window during staged rollout and add an auto-rollback if prefix hit-rate drops >15% vs baseline.
Sam: Thanks all — good catch. We'll add a short postmortem entry once staged finishes.
Tiago: Filing a quick changelog note and linking this thread to the rollback PR.
